sentences: On a day in full spring, a scholar on horseback stops right in the middle of the road.
This is Kim Hong-do's Listening to an Oriole on Horseback, and its title says exactly what is happening.
Kim Hong-do is regarded as one of the greatest painters of late Joseon.
This picture captures a person's quiet communion with nature, and it is often called the most lyrical of all Joseon genre paintings.
Start with the writing at the upper left.
It is a poem in seven-character lines about orioles over a spring river.
Its first line is usually read as saying that, beneath the flowers, the orioles sound like a thousand instruments.
After the poem comes a note that his fellow court painter Yi In-mun viewed it and Kim Hong-do painted it.
So the names of two painters of the same generation sit side by side, a record that both of them looked at this sheet.
Now look at the middle.
Kim Hong-do pushed the willow to one bank, set the little party on the road, and left almost everything else as empty paper.
This negative space fills more than half the picture.
Follow the branches of the willow on the right, up toward the top.
There, by the path, a pair of orioles is calling back and forth.
They are painted very small, yet these birds are the true subject of the whole picture.
The hanging willow fronds are made of light dots of pale ink.
If you watch their tips sway as if in a spring breeze, you may begin to feel that their gentle trembling is the birdsong itself.
Now down to the scholar's face.
He has turned his head and is looking up toward the tree.
The moment of being stopped in his tracks by a single sound is written plainly on his profile.
On the left, the boy holding the reins and even the horse seem to pause with him, so the whole picture holds its breath.
Standing in front of it, we too find ourselves listening along with them.
The road and the bank below are brushed in quickly with dark, slanting strokes of ink.
Above them, all that emptiness becomes the sky, the spring air, and the space the birdsong fills as it spreads.
Held by the Kansong Art Museum, the work was designated a Korean Treasure in 2018.
It is not a grand or showy scene; what became a national treasure is one brief moment of feeling on a country road.
Now step back and take in all that empty paper.
Close your eyes for a moment, and listen: what sound do you hear rising out of this wide blank space?
